subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Mental rehearsal is a technique used to:
options: Picture a successful performance to improve focus and reduce anxiety
questions.explain: Mental rehearsal involves visualising a successful performance to improve concentration and control nerves.

questions.q: Why might a coach set short-term goals as well as long-term goals?
options: To replace the need for training
To maintain motivation and provide a sense of progress
To make the performer give up sooner
questions.explain: Short-term goals keep motivation high and show progress towards the longer-term target.

questions.q: Above the anaerobic threshold, a performer is working:
options: Mainly aerobically with plenty of oxygen
questions.explain: Beyond the anaerobic threshold the body cannot supply enough oxygen, so it works anaerobically and lactic acid builds up.

questions.q: Which type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, usually at high pressure.

questions.q: Goal-line technology in football is an example of technology used to:
options: Give officials accurate decisions on whether the ball crossed the line
questions.explain: Goal-line technology helps officials decide accurately whether the whole ball has crossed the goal line.

questions.q: A disadvantage of the media's demand to schedule matches at certain times is that it can:
options: Be inconvenient for live spectators and disrupt players' routines
questions.explain: Media scheduling can move events to awkward times, inconveniencing fans and players to suit broadcasters.

questions.q: Why might an athlete take a stimulant such as a banned amphetamine?
options: To increase alertness and reduce tiredness
questions.explain: Stimulants increase alertness and mask fatigue, but they are banned and carry serious health risks.

questions.q: A 50-year-old's estimated maximum heart rate using the standard formula is:
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 50 = 170 bpm.

questions.q: Intrinsic motivation comes from:
options: Internal feelings of pride and satisfaction
questions.explain: Intrinsic motivation is the internal drive from enjoyment, pride and personal satisfaction.

questions.q: Why might a performer take performance-enhancing drugs such as anabolic steroids?
options: To slow their heart rate for relaxation
To increase muscle growth and train harder
questions.explain: Anabolic steroids are taken to increase muscle mass and allow harder training, but they are banned and harmful.

questions.q: On the Borg RPE (rate of perceived exertion) scale, a higher number indicates:
questions.explain: On the Borg scale, higher numbers reflect greater perceived effort and more intense exercise.

questions.q: Which is an example of extrinsic motivation?
questions.explain: Extrinsic motivation comes from external rewards such as medals, money or praise.

questions.q: In the basic information-processing model, the correct order is:
questions.explain: Information processing follows input (stimulus), decision-making, output (response) and then feedback.

questions.q: Which type of joint is the shoulder?
questions.explain: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint allowing movement in all directions.

questions.q: Anxiety in sport can be described as:
options: A negative emotional state linked to worry or nervousness
questions.explain: Anxiety is a negative emotional state involving feelings of worry, nervousness and apprehension.

questions.q: Cardiac output is calculated by multiplying:
questions.explain: Cardiac output equals stroke volume multiplied by heart rate, giving the blood pumped per minute.

questions.q: Verbal guidance is best described as:
options: Telling or explaining to a performer how to do something
questions.explain: Verbal guidance involves explaining or describing a skill using spoken words.

questions.q: A bar chart is most appropriate for comparing:
options: Separate categories such as scores for different teams
questions.explain: Bar charts are best for comparing values across separate, discrete categories.

questions.q: A 30-year-old trains in the anaerobic zone at 85% of maximum heart rate. What is their target heart rate?
Which is a drawback of sponsorship for a performer?
options: Pressure to perform and behave well to keep the sponsor
questions.explain: Sponsorship can bring pressure to perform and maintain a positive image, with funding lost if standards drop.

questions.q: Which training method involves explosive bounding, hopping and jumping to develop power?
questions.explain: Plyometric training uses explosive movements to develop muscular power.

questions.q: A performer records times of 12, 14, 14 and 16 seconds. What is the modal time?
questions.explain: The mode is the most frequently occurring value, and 14 seconds appears twice.
